Messages.Author: andrei...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
Obedience card text:

Only usable when this reacting vampire is about to enter combat with an
acting younger vampire. Untap the acting vampire. The acting vampire is
blocked, and he or she cannot attempt the same action again this turn.
(S) As above, but do not untap the acting vampire.

My question is on the definition of reacting vampire and the whole
thing with "is about to enter combat". Here's the situation:

Vamp A bum's rushes Vamp B
Vamp B blocks Vamp A and plays Obedience.

In this case combat ends before it even begins (as per card text). But
what happens if Vamp B is unable or unwilling to block?

Situation 2:
Vamp A bum's rushes Vamp B
Vamp B declares a block.
Vamp A plays stealth.
Vamp B cannot block. Combat begins? or can Vamp B play Obedience?

Is Obedience like Fast Reactions, that is the vampire must block in
order to use the card? Is a vampire that is involved in a combat and is
not the acting minion, automatically considered as the reacting minion?

Any help on this would be greatly appreciated.

Andrei Rublev.

andrei...@my-deja.com wrote:

> Obedience card text:
>
> Only usable when this reacting vampire is about to enter combat with an
> acting younger vampire. Untap the acting vampire. The acting vampire is
> blocked, and he or she cannot attempt the same action again this turn.
> (S) As above, but do not untap the acting vampire.

Card text (from the online reference):
Obedience
Cardtype: Reaction
Discipline: Dominate

Only usable when this reacting vampire is about to enter combat with an

acting younger vampire. This vampire [is not tapped] <and combat does not
occur>; untap the acting vampire. The acting vampire is blocked, and he or
she cannot attempt the same action this turn. (S) As above, but do not untap
the acting vampire.

> My question is on the definition of reacting vampire and the whole
> thing with "is about to enter combat". Here's the situation:
>
> Vamp A bum's rushes Vamp B
> Vamp B blocks Vamp A and plays Obedience.
>
> In this case combat ends before it even begins (as per card text). But
> what happens if Vamp B is unable or unwilling to block?

He can still play Obedience to end combat. Obedience doesn't make any
requirements as to blocking first. B must be untapped to play reaction
cards, though.

> Situation 2:
> Vamp A bum's rushes Vamp B
> Vamp B declares a block.
> Vamp A plays stealth.
> Vamp B cannot block. Combat begins? or can Vamp B play Obedience?

Combat would begin, and therefore B can play Obedience (if he's untapped).

> Is Obedience like Fast Reactions, that is the vampire must block in
> order to use the card?

No.

> Is a vampire that is involved in a combat and is
> not the acting minion, automatically considered as the reacting minion?

Typically, but that doesn't have any bearing on Obedience (which
makes no reference to the blocking minion or the reacting minion) nor
on Fast Reaction (which references the "blocking" minion explicitly).

Blocking minions are typically reacting minions, but not all reacting
minions are blocking minion.



After posting this question, I went to see the official rulings on this
card (what I should have done before ;).

I have to say that what you say here somewhat contradicts the rulings:

Obedience - Reaction (dom)
Is governed by the "same action" rulings. [RTR 19950509]
Will not untap an acting vampire who had been tapped when he began the
action. [RTR 19960708]
Cannot be used to avoid combat with a non-acting minion (Hidden Lurker,
for example). [LSJ 19970326]
Obedience can be played (by an untapped older vampire) to avoid the new
combat started by superior Psyche!. [LSJ 19991025]
Obedience is played after a vampire successfully blocks but before the
blocker is tapped and combat begins. It cancels combat and (in
inferior) untaps the acting minion (while the blocker does not tap).
[RTR 19991206]

The last ruling [rtr 19991206] suggests that you have to block in order
to play Obedience and not just be involved in combat.

So what's the final take on this question?

Andrei Rublev

andrei...@my-deja.com wrote:
> LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote:
> > andrei...@my-deja.com wrote:
> > > Vamp A bum's rushes Vamp B

> > > what happens if Vamp B is unable or unwilling to block?

> > He can still play Obedience to end combat. Obedience doesn't make any
> > requirements as to blocking first. B must be untapped to play reaction
> > cards, though.

> > > Is Obedience like Fast Reactions, that is the vampire must block in

> > > order to use the card?

> > No.

> After posting this question, I went to see the official rulings on this

> card (what I should have done before ;).

> I have to say that what you say here somewhat contradicts the rulings:

> [... snip ...]

> Obedience is played after a vampire successfully blocks but before the
> blocker is tapped and combat begins. It cancels combat and (in
> inferior) untaps the acting minion (while the blocker does not tap).
> [RTR 19991206]

> The last ruling [rtr 19991206] suggests that you have to block in order

> to play Obedience and not just be involved in combat.

No. The last ruling indicates that when played by a blocking vampire, it
is played after the block is successful but before the successful block
taps the blocker (this ruling is necessary since only untapped minions
can play reaction cards).

When played by a non-blocking vampire (as in the Bum's Rush example),
it is merely played before combat begins, per card text. This case is
unaffected by the ruling on how to play it when blocking.

See the cited RTR for more information about the circumstances involved
in the ruling in question.
